report:
**Conclusion:**  
Contrary to your initial view, current medical research indicates that the health claim is **true**: anti-cytokine drugs significantly reduce depressive symptoms in people with chronic inflammatory conditions.

### Key Evidence

1. **Meta-Analytic Support:** A comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical trials in chronic inflammatory diseases (such as rheumatoid arthritis, psoriasis, and inflammatory bowel disease) found that anti-cytokine agents—including anti-TNF, anti-IL-6, and anti-IL-12/23 drugs—significantly reduce depressive symptoms compared to placebo (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5794896/).
2. **Direct Antidepressant Effect:** Statistical mediation and regression analyses demonstrate that this mood improvement occurs independently of changes in primary physical disease severity or pain scores, suggesting a direct neuroimmune effect on depression rather than a simple byproduct of feeling physically better (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5794896/).
3. **Broader Immunomodulatory Evidence:** Subsequent large-scale evaluations of immunomodulatory therapies confirm that targeting pro-inflammatory cytokines consistently alleviates comorbid depressive symptoms across diverse inflammatory disorders (https://www.nature.com/articles/s41380-019-0471-8, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7244402/).

While clinical trials continue to investigate whether anti-cytokine therapies benefit major depression in individuals *without* underlying systemic inflammation, the evidence strongly supports their effectiveness for reducing depressive symptoms in patients who have chronic inflammatory conditions.

### Sources Cited

- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41380-019-0471-8
- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7244402/
